planted: Regional failover is done by updating DNS records whose time to live is 3,600 seconds, while the stated RTO for a region loss is 15 minutes.
truth: Resolvers may keep serving the old answer for up to an hour after a DNS change, so a one-hour TTL cannot meet a 15-minute RTO; the TTL, or the mechanism, or the RTO, must change.
fixed_if: the final document makes the failover mechanism and the RTO consistent (a much lower TTL, a different mechanism such as global load balancer health-based failover with no DNS dependency, or a longer RTO) instead of a 3,600-second TTL with a 15-minute RTO

planted: Three managed services are each budgeted at 99.95% availability, so the platform as a whole can achieve 99.95%.
truth: Serial dependencies multiply: 0.9995 x 0.9995 x 0.9995 is about 99.85%, so the composite cannot reach 99.95% from components at 99.95% unless redundancy beyond the services is designed in.
fixed_if: the final document no longer claims that three 99.95% components give 99.95% overall (it states the product or about 99.85%, or explains the redundancy that makes the target reachable)

planted: Each tier has a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable equal to its replica count (6 of 6), so node upgrades and drains never reduce serving capacity.
truth: A PodDisruptionBudget that allows zero voluntary disruptions blocks eviction: node drains and upgrades stall (and are eventually forced) instead of proceeding. minAvailable must be below the replica count (for example 4 of 6, or maxUnavailable 1).
fixed_if: the final document changes the budget so at least one pod can be disrupted (for example minAvailable below the replica count, or maxUnavailable of 1 or more), instead of 6 of 6

planted: The analytics team's dashboards read from the Cloud SQL high availability standby instance to keep reporting queries off the primary.
truth: The Cloud SQL high availability standby does not serve reads; it is only there for failover. Reporting reads need a read replica (or reading from BigQuery).
fixed_if: the final document no longer has dashboards read from the HA standby (it uses a read replica or BigQuery instead, or drops the claim)

planted: The BigQuery destination's data staleness limit is 15 minutes while the stated target freshness is five minutes.
truth: A staleness limit of 15 minutes allows data to be up to 15 minutes old, so the five-minute freshness target cannot be guaranteed; the setting and the target contradict each other.
fixed_if: the final document sets the staleness limit at or below the freshness target (about five minutes or less), or changes the target to match, instead of 15 minutes against five

planted: The cluster is on the Rapid release channel because it is the most stable channel and is recommended for production.
truth: Rapid gets new GKE versions first and is the least mature channel; Stable is the most conservative, and Regular is the usual production choice.
fixed_if: the final document puts the cluster on Regular or Stable (or states that Rapid is the earliest, not the most stable, channel) instead of the claim

planted: Preferred pod anti-affinity (preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution) on the hostname key guarantees that no two replicas of a tier ever share a node.
truth: Preferred anti-affinity is a soft preference and guarantees nothing; only the required form (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution) or a hard topology spread constraint on the hostname enforces it.
fixed_if: the final document no longer says a preferred anti-affinity guarantees separation (it switches to the required form or a hard spread constraint, or drops the guarantee)

planted: Restoring the most recent backup after data corruption takes about five minutes regardless of the size of the database.
truth: Restore time grows with database size; it is not constant, and a five-minute figure is unsupported for any real database.
fixed_if: the final document no longer claims a size-independent five-minute restore (it ties the estimate to database size and a tested restore time, or drops the figure)

planted: Each API pod can serve about 800 requests a second, so six replicas comfortably exceed the 5,000 requests a second peak.
truth: 6 x 800 = 4,800 requests a second, which is below the 5,000 peak even with every replica healthy, and after the loss of a zone (four replicas) it is 3,200.
fixed_if: the final document corrects the replica count or per-pod capacity so that the replicas that survive a zone loss still carry the 5,000 requests a second peak, instead of 6 x 800

planted: The pod secondary IP range is a /22 (1,024 addresses), said to be enough for 30 nodes at the default of 110 pods per node.
truth: At 110 pods per node GKE reserves a /24 (256 addresses) per node, so a /22 supports only about 4 nodes; 30 nodes would need roughly a /17.
fixed_if: the final document enlarges the pod range (about a /17 or larger for 30 nodes), or lowers max pods per node with matching arithmetic, instead of a /22 for 30 nodes
